payload.claim: No test proves `_gate_cell_suite` judges the gate cell's suite against the run's own pre-turn baseline (as the spec's notes require, to avoid census/criteria/revert degrading to `skip`). Replacing `baseline` here with an empty-prior `SuiteRun` (e.g. `type(baseline)(results=[], effective_risk=baseline.effective_risk, advisory_gates=baseline.advisory_gates)`) keeps `cell.gate_cell_runs == 1` (so the one test checking that count still passes) and still yields `outcome.state == "READY_FOR_REVIEW"`. The one test that exercises `revert` through the gate cell's third suite call, `test_revert_restores_before_committed_reads_the_tree`, cannot tell the difference: its stubbed `_revert_run_gate` (default `fails=True`) marks every name in `subset` as failed regardless of how many names are in it, so `revert_gate` returns `pass` whether `prior` is the real baseline (one new test) or empty (both tests read as 'new'), and the source paths reverted and the `order` trace are computed from `changed_files`/`test_paths`, not from `prior`, so neither differs either. A wrong (empty) baseline for the gate cell — silently worse per the task's own notes — would ship undetected.
